title: Course Schedule
description:
# Course Schedule

There are `numCourses` courses labeled from `0` to `numCourses - 1`. You are given an array `prerequisites`, where `prerequisites[i] = [ai, bi]` means you must take course `bi` before course `ai`.

Return `true` if it is possible to finish every course. Return `false` if the prerequisite graph contains a directed cycle. A self-prerequisite such as `[0,0]` is also a cycle.

For example, if course `0` requires `1` first and course `1` requires `0` first, neither can be started.

## Example 1:

**Input:** numCourses = 2, prerequisites = [[1,0]]
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** Course `0` can be taken first, then course `1`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** numCourses = 2, prerequisites = [[1,0],[0,1]]
**Output:** false
**Explanation:** Course `0` and course `1` depend on each other, so neither can be completed first.

## Constraints:

*   `1 <= numCourses <= 2000`
*   `0 <= prerequisites.length <= 5000`
*   `prerequisites[i].length == 2`
*   `0 <= ai, bi < numCourses`
*   All pairs in `prerequisites` are unique.

solutions.name: Kahn Topological Sort
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build a directed graph from each prerequisite course to the course it unlocks, and count every course's indegree. Courses with indegree `0` can be taken immediately. Each time a course is taken, remove its outgoing edges and enqueue newly unlocked courses.

## Key Insight

In an acyclic prerequisite graph, there is always at least one currently available course. If a cycle exists, the courses inside that cycle never reach indegree `0`, so the processed count stays below `numCourses`.

## Complexity Analysis

Let `V = numCourses` and `E = prerequisites.length`. Building the graph and processing every edge once costs `O(V + E)` time, and the graph, indegree array, and queue use `O(V + E)` space.

solutions.name: Three-Color DFS Cycle Detection
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build the same directed graph and mark each course with one of three states: unvisited, currently visiting, or finished. During depth-first search, reaching a currently visiting course means the current recursion path has returned to itself, so there is a cycle.

## Key Insight

The visiting state represents the active recursion stack. A finished node has already been proven to lead to no cycle, so later searches can reuse that result without exploring it again.

## Complexity Analysis

Each course changes state at most twice and each edge is inspected once. The time complexity is `O(V + E)`, and the adjacency list plus recursion stack use `O(V + E)` space.

solutions.name: Tarjan Strong Component Detection
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use Tarjan's algorithm to find strongly connected components in one DFS pass. A component with more than one course is a directed cycle. A self-edge, such as a course requiring itself, is also detected as a cycle even though its component size is one.

## Key Insight

A directed graph is a valid course schedule exactly when every strongly connected component is trivial and has no self-loop. Low-link values tell us when a whole component has been discovered.

## Complexity Analysis

Tarjan's algorithm visits each vertex and edge once. The time complexity is `O(V + E)`, and the graph, index arrays, stack, and bookkeeping use `O(V + E)` space.

solutions.name: Two-Pass Strong Component Detection
solutions.description:
## Approach

Build both the original graph and the reversed graph. First run DFS on the original graph to record courses by finish time. Then process courses in reverse finish order on the reversed graph; each traversal finds one strongly connected component. Any component with multiple courses, or any self-edge, makes the schedule impossible.

## Key Insight

This two-pass component method gives a different proof of the same graph theorem: a course schedule is feasible only when the directed prerequisite graph has no cyclic strongly connected component.

## Complexity Analysis

Both DFS passes together visit each course and edge a constant number of times. The time complexity is `O(V + E)`, and the two graphs, order list, and visited arrays use `O(V + E)` space.

tests.description: Simple prerequisite chain with no cycle.
No prerequisites means all courses can be finished.
Diamond-shaped prerequisites still have a valid topological order.
A cycle in one component blocks the schedule even when another component is acyclic.
A self-prerequisite is a directed cycle.
Multiple disconnected acyclic components can all be completed.
